summary.headline: Venus Pipes Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23.9% YoY to INR361.1 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 14.3% from 16.3% on freight costs.
summary.overview: Record quarterly revenue of INR361.1 crores (+23.9% YoY) and record exports of INR147.2 crores (41% of revenue) were driven by roughly 12% price increases and about 8% volume growth. EBITDA rose 9.1% to INR51.7 crores, but margin compressed to 14.3% as higher export freight and fuel costs hit; management said ex-price impact margin would have been about 15.5%. PAT was flat at about INR26 crores. The company completed a INR372 crore preferential allotment, of which about INR344 crores is earmarked to repay borrowings, with interest savings expected from H2 FY27. A spooling order of about INR29 crores from a data-centre customer was firmed, and the pipe order book is about INR640-670 crores.

segments.name: Seamless pipes
segments.commentary: Revenue grew around 20% YoY in Q2 FY27 per management; 54.7% of quarterly revenue. Seamless capacity utilisation above 80% in Q2, targeted above 90% in H2.

segments.name: Welded pipes
segments.commentary: Revenue grew around 20% YoY; 37.6% of quarterly revenue. Utilisation above 60% in Q2, targeted at 60-65% and then 70% in H2.

segments.name: Fittings
segments.commentary: Only about INR9 crores revenue in H1 FY27 (2.5% of Q2 revenue). Management targets INR40-50 crores in H2 at EBITDA margin of 17-20%; new capacity of about INR60 crores completed in May 2026.

segments.name: Spooling (data centre)
segments.commentary: Firm order of about INR29 crores from a data-centre customer; revenue execution started and H2 target about INR70 crores at EBITDA margin above 30%. LOI balance of about INR155-185 crores pending conversion.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Record INR147.2 crores; US was the main growth driver. Export order book is about 40% of pipe order book, with more than 50% from the US and about 40% from Europe.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pipe volume growth target of around 15%; H1 volume growth was about 8% YoY, implying stronger H2.
Management expects overall value growth of 20%-plus for the year (per analyst recap, not restated in detail).
H2 pipe EBITDA margin expected to recover toward about 16% if freight rates normalise; freight fell over the last two to three days per management.
Finance cost savings of about INR12-13 crores expected in H2 FY27 after repaying about INR344 crores of borrowings; annual saving INR28-30 crores.
FY27 capex guided at INR130-140 crores (midpoint about INR135 crores), with INR30-35 crores in H2.
Spooling LOI balance expected to convert over the next 12 months, with most orders by Q2 FY28; data-centre execution targeted before December 2027.
Data-centre spooling EBITDA margin above 30%; oil and gas 20-25%; nuclear 35-40%; power about 30%.
capex_capacity: Seamless pipe facility (second) commenced operations in May 2026; volume growth expected from it.
Fittings capacity expansion completed in May 2026; spooling operations commenced ahead of original timeline.
Capex in H1 FY27 about INR105 crores, covering spooling and fittings expansion (about INR60-65 crores), solar power plant (about INR25-30 crores) and maintenance.
New capacity being added, expected operational by January or February 2027; existing and new capacity together can deliver about INR250-300 crores annual data-centre business.
Fittings: management says revenue of 3-3.5x investment is achievable, with peak revenue of INR180-200 crores on about INR60 crores investment.
demand_pricing: Order book above INR670 crores including about INR30 crores spooling order, per the call; the pipe order book is about INR640 crores, up more than 30% YoY, and expected to execute in four to five months.
Price increases above 10% YoY and above 5% QoQ; roughly 12% of the 24% revenue growth came from price, about 8% from volume and fittings.
Demand from power, engineering, oil and gas, plus newer areas such as CNG stations, semiconductor and solar.
Europe export quota cuts of about 15-20% YoY have not materially hit Venus's European volumes, per management.
Freight pass-through is partial: some export orders have freight-band clauses, and new orders are being priced to pass costs to customers. No pass-on clause for power and fuel generally.
Power and fuel costs above 3.5% of revenue, up about 1 percentage point of sales since April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of the 24% revenue growth between price and volume?
qa_highlights.answer: About 12% from price and about 8% from volume and fittings; management targets around 15% full-year volume growth, with spooling and fittings contributing on top of pipes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per kg and margin fall?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA per kg (ex-fittings) fell to INR62 from INR64 YoY, mainly due to export freight and fuel costs; management said margins should recover in H2 if freight normalises.

qa_highlights.question: Is the capex guidance changed?
qa_highlights.answer: No change in outlook: H1 spend about INR105 crores, H2 about INR30-35 crores, so FY27 about INR130-140 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pace of spooling LOI conversion and sector expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR29 crores firm so far, with the balance of LOI (about INR155-185 crores) to convert over 12 months; sector sequence is data centres, then power, oil and gas, and nuclear.

qa_highlights.question: Where do the export order book and growth come from?
qa_highlights.answer: Of the pipe order book, more than 50% is US, about 40% Europe, the rest Middle East and others; Q2 export growth was predominantly US-led.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the next two quarters' margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects pipe margins near 16% in H2 if freight eases, plus higher-margin spooling (above 30%) and fittings (17-20%) contributions, though it said the percentage margin may optically fall as prices rise.

risks_watch: Freight and fuel cost volatility linked to Middle East conflict; margin recovery depends on freight normalisation, which management says has only started in the last few days.
Employee expense grew about 34% YoY (analyst figure); management attributed it to capacity additions, and said further increases will be modest.
Spooling LOI conversion is uncertain (only about INR29 crores firm of about INR185 crores LOI); execution timing depends on design finalisation.
Europe quota restrictions may tighten; management says exposure is limited so far.
Working capital is about 120 days of sales, with debtors around 75-80 days.
Pipe order book is about 40% export and includes project orders that may not convert, per management.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the spooling and fittings pipeline, but openly defensive on the Q2 margin drop, attributing it to freight and fuel costs. Management gave specific H2 targets but declined to quantify parts of the order book and spooling economics.
key_quotes: Excluding the impact of price increase, Q2FY27 EBITDA margin would have been ~15.5%.
We are hopeful, if this last two to three days, freight has already going towards downward trend.
Our export business achieved a new milestone, with exports reaching an all-time high of INR 147 crores and constituting 41% of revenue.

growth.why: Management targets ~15% FY27 volume growth and 20%+ value growth, with H1 volume only ~8%, so H2 must accelerate; backing is partial, citing a INR640-670 crore pipe order book (up >30% YoY), the commissioned second seamless line, fittings (INR40-50 crore H2 target) and data-centre spooling (~INR70 crore H2 target), with the spooling order firm at ~INR29 crore and LOI balance of INR155-185 crore st

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 14.3% from 16.3% on freight and fuel; management guides pipe margin back toward ~16% in H2 if freight normalises, plus spooling at >30% margin (~INR70 crore H2 target) and fittings at 17-20%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Second seamless facility commenced May 2026 and new data-centre spooling capacity is due Jan-Feb 2027, with existing plus new capacity meant to deliver INR250-300 crore annual data-centre business; seamless utilisation already above 80%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets ~15% FY27 pipe volume growth against H1 volume of only ~8% YoY, so H2 must accelerate, backed by a INR640-670 crore pipe order book (up >30% YoY) and spooling/fittings ramp.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Seamless utilisation is above 80% and targeted above 90% in H2, FY27 capex guided up to INR130-140 crore with INR30-35 crore in H2, so further capacity announcements are plausible though none is named yet.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Price increases above 10% YoY and a pipe order book up >30% support upside, but H1 volume at ~8% against a 15% target and the Q2 margin miss keep an upgrade conditional.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 margin recovery depends on freight normalisation that has only just started, spooling LOI conversion is uncertain (INR29 crore firm vs INR185 crore LOI), and a 15% volume target needs H2 acceleration from ~8% in H1.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Data-centre spooling (INR29 crore firm order, ~INR70 crore H2 target) and fittings (INR40-50 crore H2 target at 17-20% margin) ramp in H2, with sector sequence moving to power, oil and gas and nuclear afterwards.

rows.label: Spooling LOI conversion to firm orders
rows.when: next 12 months, most by Q2 FY28
rows.why: Only about INR29 crore of the roughly INR185 crore LOI is firm; the INR155-185 crore balance is expected to convert over 12 months, but execution timing depends on design finalisation.

rows.label: Interest savings from INR344 crore debt repayment
rows.why: Repaying about INR344 crore of borrowings from the INR372 crore preferential allotment is expected to save INR12-13 crore in H2 FY27 and INR28-30 crore annually.

rows.label: Pricing pass-through of freight costs
rows.why: Price increases above 10% YoY and above 5% QoQ drove about 12 points of the 24% revenue growth, and new export orders are priced to pass freight on, though power and fuel have no pass-on clause.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, the spooling and fittings pipeline, and the H2 capacity additions, but defensive on the Q2 margin drop from freight and fuel costs; analysts pressed on the price-versus-volume split and margin recovery.
